The first transmission peak is at E ≈ 0.0862 eV, found from the resonance condition of the symmetric double barrier, solved by hand.

**Setup.** The effective-mass kinetic constant is ħ²/(2m*) = 0.0380998/0.067 = 0.568654 eV nm². In the well, k = √(E/0.568654). In the barriers, κ = √((V0−E)/0.568654). The barrier width is b = 2 nm and the well width is L = 5 nm.

**Barrier reflection.** The reflection amplitude of one barrier, seen from the well side, is

r = (k²+κ²) sinh(κb) / [(k²−κ²) sinh(κb) + 2ikκ cosh(κb)].

Write the denominator's argument as θ = arg[(k²−κ²) sinh(κb) + 2ikκ cosh(κb)]. Then arg r = −θ.

**Resonance condition.** For a symmetric structure, T = 1 when the round-trip phase in the well is a multiple of 2π, so 2kL − 2θ = 2πn. For the lowest peak, n = 0, which gives kL = θ.

**Numerical solution.** Define f(E) = kL − θ.

| E (eV) | f(E) |
|---|---|
| 0.080 | −0.1155 |
| 0.086 | −0.0042 |
| 0.090 | +0.0712 |

The slope near 0.086 eV is about 0.0187 per meV. Linear extrapolation from 0.086 eV gives the root at 0.086 + 0.0042/18.7 ≈ 0.08622 eV.
